title: THE BOOK OF THE WARS OF THE LORD

sense.text:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” The book of the Lord is the Bible, and we are to seek out of it and read.

“No one of these shall fail.” Nothing written in the Bible is going to fail. Everything we read in it is going to come to pass, whether a man believes it or not. “None shall want her mate”: the Bible cannot be mated with any other book.

“For my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” These words are the Lord’s words, gathered by his spirit. So the first thing to understand before going into the wars of the Lord is this: seek out of the book of the Lord, and know that nothing in it will fail.

precepts.why:
“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” Christ comes in the volume of the book. The book of the Lord that Isaiah tells us to seek out of and read is written of him.

When we read the Bible and read that the Lord said this and the Lord did that, it is talking about Christ. He is the one that was speaking right through the scriptures, and he is the one that was dealing with us right through the scriptures. Seek ye out of the book of the Lord: it is written of me. That is him, that is the Lord, right there.

“For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” Moses wrote of Christ. When you read Genesis, Exodus, Numbers and Deuteronomy, the one Moses was writing about when he wrote that the Lord said and the Lord did, was always Christ.

“But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” So the Lord of the book of the Lord is Christ, and that is the key to everything that follows: the Lord who fought for Israel in the books of Moses is Christ.

sense.text:
“Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord.” This is where the topic comes from. There was a book that was called the book of the wars of the Lord, a book of nothing but the wars of the Lord, and we do not have that book today. But by reading the other scriptures the picture can be put together: the wars of the Lord that took place back then, and the war that is going to take place in the future when he returns.

“What he did in the Red sea”: that is in Exodus. All of what is read here goes back to when we came out of Egypt and when we were conquering the land, and the Lord was there fighting with us.

And who is the Lord in the book of the wars of the Lord? Christ. Christ is not only going to war in the future. He has been warring ever since the beginning, ever since Exodus. There was a whole book that went into the times the Lord fought for us, and accounts of those wars are still found in the books we have.

“And at the stream of the brooks that goeth down to the dwelling of Ar, and lieth upon the border of Moab. And from thence they went to Beer.” All of this is the journey out of Egypt, the same history told in Exodus.

Esdras hears a voice out of a bush, the same way the Lord revealed himself unto Moses in the bush “when my people served in Egypt.” The Lord brought Moses up to the mount, held him a long season, “and told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end.”

“These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” Some things Moses hid. He hid them by writing them in parables and similitudes, so that not everybody could understand them. Only the wise could understand.

“I will go, as thou hast commanded me, and reprove the people which are present”: Esdras would correct the people of his own time, when we came out of the captivity of the Persians and the Medes. “But they that shall be born afterward, who shall admonish them?” Those born afterward, in the future, is us today. Who is going to tell them what to do? “The world is set in darkness, and they that dwell therein are without light”: there is wickedness on the earth.

“For thy law is burnt.” At that time the scriptures were burnt. Our forefathers grew up in Babylon for seventy years; the scrolls were destroyed, many of the laws were forgotten, and when you read Nehemiah and Esdras you see they were not even keeping Tabernacles or God’s laws.

“Therefore no man knoweth the things that are done of thee”: nobody knew the things God had done, like delivering us out of Egypt and the wars of the Lord. Esdras knew, because he was brought up in the law. “Or the works that shall begin” is what is going to happen in the future, the prophecies and what we have to hope for, and the people did not know it.

“Send the Holy Ghost into me, and I shall write all that hath been done in the world since the beginning.” Esdras wrote over everything that Moses wrote, because by the time we came out of the captivity everything had been destroyed and our people did not know how to serve God. The Lord put the spirit on Esdras and he wrote back everything word for word.

“That men may find thy path”: that is how we are able to find the path today. We all came together because we heard the word of God. “And that they which will live in the latter days may live”: that is us.

The Lord would light a candle of understanding in Esdras’ heart, “which shall not be put out.” “Some things shalt thou publish, and some things shalt thou shew secretly to the wise.” What he published is what you read in Nehemiah and Esdras, when Esdras opened the book of the law, read it distinctly and gave the sense, teaching Israel all over again what the Lord did for them, and the people wept, listening from morning till night.

“Our fathers at the beginning were strangers in Egypt, from whence they were delivered: and received the law of life, which they kept not.” The land of Sion was parted among us by lot, but our fathers did unrighteousness, and as a righteous judge “he took from you in time the thing that he had given you”: he took the land back from us.

“If so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive”: if you change your evil ways you will be kept alive, “and after death ye shall obtain mercy.” That is something heavy: after you die, you will obtain mercy.
“For after death shall the judgment come, when we shall live again: and then shall the names of the righteous be manifest, and the works of the ungodly shall be declared.”

Esdras was up there forty days, the same way Moses went up to Mount Sinai for forty days. Esdras was learning everything the Lord taught Moses, and he wrote down word for word everything Moses gave us that the people had forgotten.

He drank a cup “full as it were with water, but the colour of it was like fire,” and “my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

The spirit strengthened his memory. The only way the spirit can strengthen your memory is if there is something there. Sometimes in the heat of battle at camp a scripture you read two years ago comes right to your mind; that is what the Holy Spirit does. But it cannot strengthen a memory that has nothing in it. Esdras had read the whole law many times, so his memory could be strengthened to remember everything word for word and write it down, and even much more.

“The Highest gave understanding unto the five men, and they wrote the wonderful visions of the night that were told, which they knew not”: they were writing visions they did not understand, forty days, writing in the day and eating bread at night.

“In forty days they wrote two hundred and four books.” Today we have 80 books: 39 in the Old Testament, 14 in the Apocrypha and 27 in the New Testament. Take away the New Testament, because it came afterward, and that leaves 53. Out of the 204 books Esdras wrote, 151 books are missing. With the 27 of the New Testament, there should be 231 books in all.

“The first that thou hast written publish openly, that the worthy and unworthy may read it.” The first set of books goes into the law. Everybody has to hear the law and learn the law, so it was given for the worthy and the unworthy to read.

“But keep the seventy last, that thou mayest deliver them only to such as be wise among the people: for in them is the spring of understanding.” There were seventy books with heavy things in them, a different level of wisdom and understanding, that only wise men could read.

The Most High made it so that we do not have those seventy books today, because there are things in them we are not supposed to know yet; they would mess with some of our minds. The important books he made sure we got. Some of those other books are most likely held down in the Vatican City, where they have whole cities of books underground. One who was sent into the basement of the Vatican said they brought out the Maccabees, Esther and the Wisdom of Solomon, books that were not in the Bible, and that there are many more down there. They have our books. But what we have is enough to get the kingdom. The Lord allowed that too: there were things in those books that were plain, and some had to be taken away so the lie could be spread on the earth. He wants us just to trust in him.

precepts.why:
“And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher?” So there is a book of Jasher, part of the scriptures, that we do not have today. That is one of the books Esdras wrote over.

The book of Jasher that is put out on the Bible apps today is not that book; it was made up. It contradicts the Bible, and the books of the prophets do not contradict one another, they complement each other. A book talking about angels having sex with women or Esau being saved is a book Esau made up to throw us off. The real one is kept, along with others, in the Vatican, while misinformation is put out to confuse.

So leave the book of Jasher, Enoch and the rest of them alone. Be not deceived: evil communication corrupts. Read that stuff and thoughts start coming to your mind, and they came from that book. Stay with what the Lord gave us.

“Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” There was a book called the chronicles of the kings of Judah, and we do not have that book. It is another proof of what the Lord told Esdras: books were written that are not in our hands today.

“And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.” There is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Israel. We do not have that today either.

“And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?” There is a book called the acts of Solomon, a book you would love to read.

But some of those books are full of the spring of wisdom and understanding. Things Solomon revealed there, the Lord did not want us to know today, so he made it so that those books are not in our possession.

“Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel.”

We do have the prayer of Manasseh; it is in the Apocrypha. But that prayer was also part of the book of the kings of Israel, and that book we do not have.

“Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer.” We have the book of Samuel. But do we have a book of Nathan the prophet? A book of Gad the seer? Nathan wrote a book in which the Lord showed him certain things, and so did Gad, and we are missing them.

Those are the books the Lord told Esdras to show only to the wise, because there are things in them that not everybody can understand, things the Lord did not want everybody to know.

“Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?” Nathan the prophet is another book we were supposed to have. Ahijah the Shilonite was a prophet who wrote things we know nothing about. Iddo the seer is another: a seer is a prophet, one who sees the future.

Those prophets went into some heavy things. Why did Judas Maccabeus, the woman with the seven sons, and our forefathers in the days of Antiochus think the way they did, ready to die, some saying they would rather die in their innocency than fight on the sabbath? Because they had a level of understanding they got from those seventy books. They understood things, like regeneration, that we are only starting to figure out piece by piece today.

“His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him,” “behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers.” So there was a book called the sayings of the seers, and we do not have it today.

The Lord took those books away. Some things in them we are not to understand today; he wants us to trust in him.

“But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.” After Christ died and went up, he told John to let everybody know: what you have, hold fast to it till I come. What we have today is 80 books. Do not go looking for other books. Esau made up a lot of the books out there, like a book of Lilith, Adam’s second wife. Do not try to mate them with the scriptures. Leave them alone; some brothers can handle them and some cannot, and it is not worth the chance. That is what those books do: bug your mind out.

What is in those 80 books is enough to get the kingdom: all the laws, thou shalt not, and the prophecies of what is going to take place. Even though the Vatican took the other books and hid them, the Lord allowed it, keeping what he did back then from us for now.

“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations.” If you overcome your lust, the temptations and the white man’s lies, and hold on to that little faith and understanding you got from these 80 books, you are going to rule the nations. You have enough to get the kingdom.

“For now we see through a glass, darkly.” The glass we see through darkly is the Bible. Remember what God told Moses: some things you are to hide. So we get bits and pieces; one apostle explains it here and another there, and we are putting together the full picture, but we are still seeing in pieces. We do not have all the books, but we have enough to get the kingdom.

“But then face to face.” When Christ comes, he is going to teach us face to face. The other things, those seventy books he told Esdras to show only to the wise, he is going to let us know. Whatever you are confused about now, the Lord will make it clear.

“Now I know in part.” That is why you will never hear us say we understand everything or have one hundred percent of the truth: we know in part. The part we have is these 80 books, and the Most High has it that way because our flesh cannot contain some of these things. “But then shall I know even as also I am known”: when Christ returns, we are going to understand everything.

sense.text:
“Behold, the day of the Lord cometh.” The day of the Lord is destruction, and this is going to happen in World War III, in the third woe.

“And thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee.” Our spoil, the land of Israel, is divided right now, with Arabs over there and Caucasians over there.

The book of the wars of the Lord is one of the books we do not have, but we are able to go into the scriptures and see it in part, because there is record of those wars in the other books.

“For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle.” That is the prophecy: all nations are going to be gathered against that land, because of the evil the synagogue of Satan over there is doing. What Trump is doing now and all the conflicts happening over there, and the evil done to the Arabs, are going to cause a war in which the Muslims come together and go down into that land, then Europe and all nations go down there, and it starts the third war.

“And the city shall be taken”: the Arabs will take that city; that is future prophecy. “And the houses rifled, and the women ravished”: the women over there will be raped. “And half of the city shall go forth into captivity”: prisoners of war.

“Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations.” After the Arabs take the city and the world war breaks out and America is destroyed, Christ returns, and then they fight against him. He is going to fight against Europe, against America, against the Arabs.

“As when he fought in the day of battle.” When did the Lord fight in the day of battle? That is the book of the wars of the Lord. He will go forth and fight against the nations in the future the same way he fought against the nations in the past, when he brought us out of Egypt, which was the day of battle, and when we conquered the land. He is going to throw down the same way, as was written in the book of the wars of the Lord of what he did in the Red sea and in the brooks of Arnon.

“The Lord is a man of war.” Some read that and pull out only that the Lord is a man and he loves war. Moses is saying much more. Moses said it because he saw the Lord warring and fighting for his people.

“The Lord is his name.” This Lord is Christ, the anointed. That is who it is talking about when it says the Lord is a man of war.

“Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.” It is telling you what he did: he destroyed Pharaoh, his chariots, his men, his armies. Who did that? The Lord. “The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone.”

“Thy right hand, O Lord, hath dashed in pieces the enemy.” This is the wars of the Lord we are reading about: the Lord fighting against the Egyptians and killing them, drowning them in the Red sea, bringing plagues upon them.

precepts.why:
Some might still say the Lord here is the Father. Solomon gives the same account Moses gave. “For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war.”

Who is the word of God? Christ. He has a throne in the heavens, and during Exodus he leaped off his throne and came down for war. That is why Moses says the Lord is a man of war. It was the word of God that came down in the Passover and killed all those Egyptians and drowned them in the Red sea. The Lord was warring.

“Into the midst of a land of destruction, And brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death.” A lot of people do not understand what Passover is really about. It is about death and the destruction of our enemies.

“Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for.” The Lord was sending the Egyptians horrible visions and dreams. “And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.” The Lord was afflicting them, warring with them.

“The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” The Lord from heaven is Christ. He is the almighty word that leaped off his throne and came down and killed all those Egyptians in Exodus. That is why Moses says the Lord is a man of war.

sense.text: “And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel.” Even though the Lord had killed all the firstborn in Egypt and filled Egypt with death, Pharaoh still went after the Israelites; but it was the Lord who made him do it.

“They were sore afraid,” and they turned on Moses: “Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness?” This is how rebellious black people are; our people will turn on you quick.

“Is not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians?” We told you in Egypt, leave us alone, we don’t want to leave Egypt; some of us got good jobs. God damn, that’s how black people is. That is how our people think today: you Israelites, leave me alone, I don’t want to hear that. Some are comfortable being slaves. Some love being a servant, serving the white man and the nations, getting up every morning to that 9 to 5, making good money, comfortable in America, the same way some of our people were comfortable in ancient Egypt. “For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.”

“Fear ye not, stand still”: the people were running, and Moses said stop running, “and see the salvation of the Lord.” “The Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever”: all of them dead.

“The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.” This is the lesson, the book of the wars of the Lord. When we came out of Egypt, this was one of the wars of the Lord, where the Lord was fighting for us.

“I will get me honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host.” The Lord wanted honour. He wanted to flex his power. He hardened the Egyptians’ hearts to make them chase after Israel into the sea, so that he could kill all of them, hundreds of thousands, and get his honour, so they would know: don’t mess with me and my people. So the whole world would talk about what he did to these damn Egyptians; and to this day they are still talking about it. “And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord”: don’t play with me; I told you, let my people go.

“The pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel.” That cloud is a chariot. It came and stood between them to protect Israel as they crossed the sea. Imagine seeing something like what they call a UFO today come and stand between you; the Egyptians were afraid.

“It was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these: so that the one came not near the other all the night.” Who was doing that? The Lord.
“The Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind.” Moses stretched out his hand, but it was the Lord with Moses who made the sea go back.

“The Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubled the host of the Egyptians, And took off their chariot wheels.” The Egyptians themselves said, “Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.”
“The Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.” The Lord killed all those Egyptians in the sea; “there remained not so much as one of them.”

“Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.” This is the wars of the Lord. The Lord saved Israel, and we saw them all dead.

“And Israel saw that great work which the Lord did upon the Egyptians: and the people feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses.” When they saw what the Lord did, they believed: my God is real. That is the Passover we celebrate.

So when Zechariah says the Lord will fight as when he fought in the day of battle, it goes back to this. This was one of the times the Lord fought for us, and accounts like this were written in the book of the wars of the Lord.

precepts.why:
“All our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea.” That cloud is a chariot. And Paul is speaking to the Corinthians, saying all our fathers passed through the sea; so the Corinthians were Israel. Some will say there was a mixed multitude, but the mixed multitude all died in the wilderness, lusting after evil things. If the wicked of our own people did not make it, the mixed multitude did not either.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”: Moses taught us God’s laws. “And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. That rock, that chariot following us, was Christ. And who killed the Egyptians? Christ.

“And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light.” Who went before them in the pillar of cloud? Christ, the rock that followed them, and that pillar of cloud is a chariot. “He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night.”

That cloud following them day and night was the Lord inside it. Scripture calls him the Lord, and when we read about the Lord it was always Christ, as he said: I come in the volume of the book, Moses wrote of me. He came down and smote the Egyptians, the same way he is going to come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt that we are living in today.

sense.text:
“Did ever people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as thou hast heard, and live?” How did the Lord take us out of Egypt? By war.

“Or hath God assayed to go and take him a nation from the midst of another nation.” The same is happening today: we are becoming a nation in the midst of a nation. The children of Israel became a nation in ancient Egypt; we were destroyed and brought here, and we are becoming a nation again in spiritual Egypt, as Daniel 2 says, in the days of these kings shall a kingdom be set up that shall not be destroyed. And the same way the Egyptians saw us multiplying and dealt wisely with us and oppressed us, it is going to be the same thing again in the future.

“By temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war.” The signs are the plagues the Lord brought on Egypt, and the wonders are what Moses did in Egypt through the Lord. How did the Lord take us out of Egypt? By war. When it says the Lord is a man of war, when he came to deliver us out of Egypt it was war; he was warring with the Egyptians.

“And by a mighty hand, and by a stretched out arm, and by great terrors.” The Lord brought terror on the Egyptians when we came out of Egypt, “before your eyes.”

“Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice.” Whose voice did they hear from heaven? Christ’s. He is the one who came down and gave us the commandments. “That he might instruct thee: and upon earth he shewed thee his great fire.” That great fire is his shape. When the Lord came down in Exodus 20 to give the commandments, everybody saw a great fire; only the seventy elders saw his majesty. “And thou heardest his words out of the midst of the fire”: he was speaking the commandments and the earth was shaking, and the people were terrified and said, we don’t want God to speak to us; Moses, you tell us.

When he came down on the earth all you saw was a flame of fire, which goes back to his throne, with fire issuing forth from it.

precepts.why:
Some think the voice heard in the wilderness was the Father’s. “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.”

No time in history did we hear the Father’s voice or see his shape. So the voice our people heard in the wilderness was Christ’s, and the shape we saw in the wilderness was Christ. That is who was speaking and who gave us the commandments.

Paul mentions the same thing. “See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth.” The one that spoke on earth is Moses. The people said, we don’t want to hear God lest we die; Moses, you tell us. Moses gave us the laws, we refused them from Moses, and everybody was killed in the wilderness. “Much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven”: the one speaking from heaven was the Lord.

“Whose voice then shook the earth.” His voice shook the earth, and that is why the people did not want to hear him. “But now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.” He is going to shake nations when he returns in the future. The Lord already knew we would go off and that he would have to come again and deliver us.

“For our God is a consuming fire.” Paul says it because that is what the people saw: all fire. The Lord said do not let anybody come near the mountain when I come down, or they die. When he came down it was a consuming fire, and that is all anyone saw except the seventy elders, who had the Holy Spirit on them.

sense.text:
“So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” There can be no salvation without your enemy being destroyed. The same way the Lord came down and destroyed all our enemies in ancient Egypt, that is what salvation is: the Lord coming to save you from your enemies. Some of you are trying to save your enemy. Salvation is not your enemies getting saved; salvation is your enemies being destroyed.

That is what the Passover is about. When we celebrate the Passover, it goes into the wars of the Lord: the Lord making war on the Egyptians, destroying them and saving you.

The thing is, our people do not know who their enemies are. Black people, Hispanics, Colombians, Puerto Ricans, Dominicans thinking the Haitians are their enemies: your enemies are the people that enslaved you and are oppressing you. Imagine Moses coming to deliver the children of Israel and the Israelites trying to save the Egyptians; that is what is happening today, when people say God came to save the Egyptians as well. That makes no sense.

precepts.why:
“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people.” His people is the Israelites; it is possessive. “That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us.”

Who is your enemy, black man, black woman? Some are scared to say it, scared to lose their jobs, and say their enemy is the spiritual demon Satan. Yes, Satan is your enemy, but he works with his children, and his children is the Caucasian race. And not only the white man: the Arabs and all nations are going to pay for what they did to our people. Teach your children that these people do not love you; they are your enemy. From the mother’s womb we have been fighting with them, and that is why they hate us so much. We live in a false illusion that everybody is equal and everybody loves everybody, but we are at the bottom of society.

Christ came to save us from our enemies because our enemies enslaved us, destroyed us, scattered us in slavery and took our land. All nations hate us. “To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham.”

“That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear.” That is salvation, and that is Passover: us being delivered from the hand of our enemies. Today we are in the hands of our enemies, and Christ is going to return and redeem us from them, and for that to happen they all have to die, the same way the Lord drowned all the Egyptians in the sea.

We serve him with fear today. In ancient Egypt, when we asked to go and sacrifice, Pharaoh said we had too much idle time and gave us more work. It is the same with a man asking for a day off and fearing his boss will fire him. Delivered, we shall serve him without fear, “In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.”

sense.text:
“For in all things, O Lord, thou didst magnify thy people, and glorify them.” In all things the Lord magnified his people, the twelve tribes of Israel. “Neither didst thou lightly regard them: but didst assist them in every time and place.”

God assisted us in every time and wherever we were. The Lord was always there fighting for us, and even in these last days the Lord will help us.

“Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude.” Don’t be scared of people, armies or anybody. Teach the word of God and speak the word of God no matter what people say or what they threaten you with.

“For the battle is not yours, but God’s.” The battle belongs to the Lord because the Lord is always there fighting with you, even when you cannot see him.

precepts.why:
This is for those with weak faith who do not believe the Lord is with them and fighting with them. “Behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?” A whole army came for this one prophet.

It is going to be the same thing in the future: federal agents and DEA agents will surround the houses of some of us. Eventually they will come for the ones teaching this too. That is the mind you have to have. You are not going to teach the word of God and have everything be good.

“Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” As men of God, realize the Lord is always with you, and stronger are they that are with you than they that are with the enemy. “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see.” “And, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire.” Those chariots are angels, waiting for the word. Men’s army surrounded Elisha, and the Lord’s army surrounded that army.

You cannot see it, but the Lord and his angels are with us, fighting with us. Even in your evil the angels are there writing down everything you do. There is no way we could do what the Lord sent us to do on the earth, no way IUIC and Israel could grow, unless he is with us.

“Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh.” Christ came and died; the Romans crucified him, lynched him, beat him. He suffered for us. “Arm yourselves likewise with the same mind.”

If your mind is not that you are going to suffer the same way Christ suffered, you are not a soldier in Christ. The Bible tells you what is going to happen. An army will surround the house, they will lie and call you a terrorist, and the federal agents are watching, waiting to set you up. Remember COINTELPRO; that did not stop. We are going up against a wicked, evil people who will put you away for the rest of your life knowing you did not do it, because they do not want to hear the teachings of Christ. So arm your mind.

“For he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin.” That is how you become perfect: you go through things and suffer in the flesh. If you want a good life, this truth is not for you.

sense.text: The Lord fought for us in every time. “And the Lord said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee.” The Lord was always fighting for us, always with us, warring with the nations: I will be with you and make sure you slaughter every last one of them.

“Joshua therefore came unto them suddenly, and went up from Gilgal all night.” “And the Lord discomfited them before Israel, and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon.” The Lord was fighting with Joshua.

“The Lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them.” This is the wars of the Lord, the Lord warring with the nations; this is one of the events from the book of the wars of the Lord. “They were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword”: the Lord killed more than all that we killed, picking off these heathens with hailstones, the Lord pelting down hailstones on the Canaanites that were in the land.

“Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.” “And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies.” Through the Lord, Joshua stopped time, and we were able to destroy all our enemies. Some say that sounds like a fairy tale; those who believe, that faith is going to take you to another level.

“Is not this written in the book of Jasher?” We do not have the book of Jasher today. “So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.”

“And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the Lord hearkened unto the voice of a man.” Joshua was a godly man, and when he said sun, stand still, the Lord did it for him because of his faith. He was not doubting; he believed the Lord would stop the sun.

“For the Lord fought for Israel.” This is the book of the wars of the Lord: the Lord was fighting for us.
The five kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah, afraid of Joshua and his God, who stopped the day. “Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave, and set men by it for to keep them.”

“And stay ye not, but pursue after your enemies, and smite the hindmost of them; suffer them not to enter into their cities.” Joshua was a real warrior, not a man to play with, and he was an Ephraimite, what is called a Puerto Rican today. What we are reading about is war: Israel taking the land of Canaan, destroying the people of the land, conquering the land of Israel.

They made an end of slaying them “with a very great slaughter.” “None moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel”: when the heathen saw time stop and hailstones come out of heaven, nobody spoke against us, because our God was fighting with us.
“Bring out those five kings unto me out of the cave”: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon. This is us taking the land.

“Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. And they came near, and put their feet upon the necks of them.” That is how bad Joshua was: bring them kings down, get on the floor, put your foot upon their necks. Hey boy, you think I would not catch you? All that crap you was talking. This is what the Bible is about; this is what a man of God is about.

“Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the Lord do to all your enemies against whom ye fight.” Everybody you fight against, your foot is going to be on their necks, and that is going to happen again in the future.
“And afterward Joshua smote them, and slew them, and hanged them on five trees.” All that talk, and now all of them dead. “And they were hanging upon the trees until the evening.”

“And all these kings and their land did Joshua take at one time, because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.” The Lord God of Israel fought for us. That is the wars of the Lord: every time, he was there fighting with us.

precepts.why:
“And Joshua at that time turned back, and took Hazor.” “There was not any left to breathe: and he burnt Hazor with fire.” This is us conquering the land. “He utterly destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the Lord commanded”: he killed everything when he went into the land, and he was not playing.

“There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel.” “For it was of the Lord to harden their hearts, that they should come against Israel in battle, that he might destroy them utterly.”

Joshua “cut off the Anakims from the mountains.” The Anakims are the giants, so Joshua was fighting giants and destroyed them utterly. “Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, there remained”: Gaza is the Philistines, where Goliath came from; only there were giants left.

“So Joshua took the whole land,” “and Joshua gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes.” He divided the land among the twelve tribes. These are the wars of the Lord.

sense.text: Joshua saw “a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand,” and Joshua stepped to him: “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?”
“Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Who is the captain of the host of the Lord? This is Christ.

precepts.why:
“But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death.” He came a little lower than the angels when he came the last time. Before that, in Exodus, he did not come lower than an angel; he came down like an angel.

“To make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.” The captain of their salvation is the captain of the host of the Lord, the Lord of armies, that Joshua saw in Joshua 5. That was Christ who was there.

sense.text: “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel.” When we fight and when we war, we war in the name of our God, the Lord of hosts.

“This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee.” This is the Philistine, Gaza, Goliath, a giant, one of the Anakims that was left. We read how Joshua was rolling; now David: I am coming in the name of the Lord, and I am going to kill you and take your head. “And I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air”: David was violent. “That all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.”
“For the battle is the Lord’s.” The battle belongs to the Lord. Anytime you go to war, it is the Lord that is with you fighting.

precepts.why:
“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war.” David understood that the Lord was with him in every fight and battle he was in, and it was the Lord teaching him how to fight. David did not go to any kung fu school. He chased a lion and killed it, he fought bears; he could do it because the Lord was with him.

The Lord is our strength. That is how you learn to war: you cannot war without the Lord warring with you. “And my fingers to fight”: to punch a man and break his teeth. Not that you should be doing that to anybody today, unless you are defending yourself.

“And when David enquired of the Lord.” David used to talk to the Lord: Lord, should I go up now, should I do this? We have to learn to do that. Before you make a decision, talk to the Lord and ask him to show you what is right, and if it is not right, to shut it down. Sisters, do that before marrying these brothers; brothers, do it too. The Lord does hear you; you are not talking to yourself.

“Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” This goes back to the Lord teaching David how to war: don’t go right now; go around and come up behind them.

“And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself.” When you hear me going on top of the mulberry trees, rush them. “For then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines”: I am going before you, I am there fighting with you. These are the wars of the Lord.

When you read the Maccabees, angels came down and fought with Judas Maccabeus, shielding him so nobody could hit him.

sense.text: “And in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” Christ is coming back, and in righteousness he is going to judge and he is going to make war. This is the wars of the Lord that are going to take place in the future, the fighting of Zechariah 14.
“His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.” Only he knows that name.

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood.” His garment is dipped in blood because the Lord will be warring; enough nations are going to be slaughtered. “And his name is called The Word of God.” Remember the almighty word that leaped down from his throne into a land and brought death: that is not only back then, it is talking about the future too.

“And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” When Christ comes back, he is coming with the armies of heaven. He is not coming back to shake hands. He is coming back for war, for deliverance, for vengeance.

“And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations.” Christ is not using a literal weapon to kill; he is using his words. He is not coming to save the nations; he is coming to destroy the nations. “And he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God”: treading them down.
“KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.” He is the Lord of all the lords.

“Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God.” Christ is the great God, and the supper he is making is men’s flesh. When a war takes place, the vultures come to eat the dead bodies: “the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men,” “both free and bond, both small and great.” This is Christ coming back and doing all that killing. This is the war of the Lord.

“And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army.” The beast is the seven heads and ten horns, the fourth beast that rules this earth: Europe and America, the white man. The kings of the earth are the Arabs and all the kings of the earth. They are not going to hug and kiss Christ when he returns; they will fight against him. The white man is really going to believe he can fight against Christ and the 144,000.

“And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet.” That fourth kingdom ruling the earth today will be destroyed, and the false prophet is Christianity. Everybody that worships the white man and his lies, the white man as Jesus, the white man as a Jew, has the mark of the beast. “These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone”: that is eternal damnation.
“And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth.” This is Christ; the remnant are killed by the sword from his mouth.

precepts.why:
Who are the armies following him? “Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints.” Those are the armies: the saints with the white robes, the 144,000, coming for vengeance. Christ is coming back with his top Gs, those brothers that loved not their lives unto death and received their immortal bodies. The fine linen, white and clean, is the immortal body.

“To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds,” “and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.” The Lord is coming for vengeance.

sense.text: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat.” This is the war of the Lord: he is going to bring everybody down there into the land of Israel. “And will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations”: they scattered us in slavery. “And parted my land”: they took our land, the Palestinians and the white man.

“Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war.” This is what God says we are to proclaim among the Gentiles. Let the Arabs, the Chinese, America and Europe know: there will be no peace. Prepare war, because the Lord God is a man of war. “Wake up the mighty men”: all of you who think you are bad, who know karate and kung fu and can shoot a gun, all you warriors in Iran, in America, in Europe. “Let all the men of war draw near”: come down to Jerusalem.

“Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears”: the farmer too is getting drafted. “Let the weak say, I am strong”: yes we can fight against the God of Israel, that black man that comes out of the sky; we have nuclear bombs.

“Assemble yourselves, and come, all ye heathen, and gather yourselves together round about”: surround me. “Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.”

The war of Armageddon is in the land of Israel. First the Arabs fight over there and take the land, as in Zechariah 14. All nations come down. America’s army is destroyed over there, then America the country is destroyed, and the war goes on. In the midst of America being destroyed, Christ returns, and they leave the war they are fighting with each other and come against Christ, in the land of Israel, in the valley of Jehoshaphat. You have the valley of Megiddo and the valley of Jehoshaphat. The American military will still be intact, and Europe and everybody will come together to fight against Christ. The Lord wants it that way; he wants them to come down so he can flex on them.

“Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe.” “For their wickedness is great”: the wickedness of the white man and the nations is great. “Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision”: multitudes of heathen coming down there.

“The Lord also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem.” That is where he is coming back and touching down. “And the heavens and the earth shall shake”: the nations are going to shake.

“So shall ye know that I am the Lord your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more.” Nobody is going to occupy that land anymore; no Caucasian over there saying I am a Jew.

“Egypt shall be a desolation.” The Egypt here is America, spiritual Egypt; this place is going to be destroyed. “And Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land”: because of the evil they are going to do to us here in America. We do nothing to these people but teach them the word of God, and they will kill us and put us in prison.
“But Judah shall dwell for ever.” “For I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed”: God is going to cleanse our blood. “For the Lord dwelleth in Zion.”

“The noise of a multitude in the mountains, like as of a great people.” That multitude is the same one read in Joel. “A tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together”: gathered together in the valley of Jehoshaphat. “The Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle”: the Lord of hosts gathering them together.

“They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, even the Lord.” The end of heaven is paradise; the Lord is coming from paradise, “and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.”

“Howl ye; for the day of the Lord is at hand; it shall come as a destruction from the Almighty.” Everybody is going to be scared: “every man’s heart shall melt.” “Their faces shall be as flames”: that says something heavy.
“Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate.” It is going to be a cruel day.

The Lord will fight for us the same way he fought in the day of battle, and this is that. “That man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven”: that is Christ with his saints. “When he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seen under him.”

“And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice.” That is the two-edged sword. When Christ speaks, he speaks the word of God: Thou shalt not commit adultery, and men burn up; Thou shalt not kill, and men burn up. Our God is a devouring fire.

“There was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” All nations, all the armies, saying, let’s go fight against the King of kings, that black man that comes out of the sky; he is an alien, like Independence Day. They literally think they can fight against our King when he returns.

“All they which were gathered together to subdue him were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.” The wars of the Lord: all the armies of the earth, Europe, America, the Arabs, the Persians, will be afraid and still fight.

“As he saw the violence of the multitude that came, he neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war.” They will be shooting Hellfire missiles, thousands of missiles and nuclear bombs at him, and he will not even lift a hand. “But only I saw that he sent out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire, and out of his lips a flaming breath, and out of his tongue he cast out sparks and tempests.” All he does is open his mouth and speak the word of God, like a firestorm going out of his mouth.

It “fell with violence upon the multitude which was prepared to fight, and burned them up every one”: all the armies of the earth, Europe, America, China, Japan. “Nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.”

“The same is he whom God the Highest hath kept a great season, which by his own self shall deliver his creature: and he shall order them that are left behind.” Those left behind are those of us who were not killed.
“That he held neither sword, nor any instrument of war, but that the rushing in of him destroyed the whole multitude that came to subdue him.” They rush into him, and he destroys the whole multitude.

“The most High will begin to deliver them that are upon the earth”: the Lord will begin to deliver his sons, the twelve tribes of Israel on the earth. “And he shall come to the astonishment of them that dwell on the earth,” because they are not expecting a black man to come out of the sky. “One city against another, one place against another, one people against another”: this is the third war.

“And then shall my Son be declared”: Christ is going to return. When the people hear his voice they leave the battle against one another, and an innumerable multitude gathers “to overcome him by fighting. But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion.”

“And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations.” The wicked inventions are their missiles, guns, nuclear weapons, tanks and intercontinental ballistic missiles; the Lord is going to rebuke all of them. They “for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest”: that tempest is the fire that comes out of his mouth, like a hurricane of fire.

“And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented.” That is when torment begins: when the Lord returns and kills you with that fire. It is not regular fire. Your body is gone, but your soul is still burning. “And he shall destroy them without labour by the law”: he will be speaking the law of God, and that is what is going to be killing people.

“The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war.” That is the man of war of Exodus: the Lord is a man of war. “He shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies.” His enemies are Europe, America, China, the Arabs, all nations, and the wicked Israelites too.

“I have long time holden my peace; I have been still, and refrained myself.” The Lord saw all the evil done on this earth and said nothing; he had to restrain himself while the white man was murdering, killing and enslaving his people. “Now will I cry like a travailing woman; I will destroy and devour at once”: now he is going to let loose on all the heathen and devour their armies at once.
“I will make waste mountains and hills”: he is going to destroy nations.

“And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not; I will lead them in paths that they have not known.” The Lord is going to bring us by a way we did not know; there are paths we have not known. “I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight”: everything crooked is going to be made straight. “These things will I do unto them”: unto us.

“When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee.” All of this history of God fighting for us as a people is written so that we have faith and hope for when the time comes that we must endure. “When thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned”: God is going to be with us, and we have to get that confidence from now.

“For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom.” He killed the Egyptians for us, and he is doing the same thing today: he has already started on modern Egypt, the Arabs and the fake Jews, for us.

“Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee.” God loves us and will hear our affliction when they come to persecute us: I will kill people for you.

“Fear not: for I am with thee.” Just as when Pharaoh came to persecute us while God was delivering us out of Egypt, when the persecution comes a lot of us are going to be scared. But God is with us, and we have to know that. “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west”: from the east side of the planet and from the western hemisphere.
“Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” His sons are the Israelites scattered throughout the planet. This is the new Passover; this is deliverance.
